name: manual_034b17
claim: For periscope (diazMelgarejo/periscope): the repo has two closely-related but genuinely distinct branches, main and merged, and confusing them is a real, demonstrated failure mode, not theoretical. A fresh git clone defaults to main. Confirmed directly this session: main can be genuinely far behind merged (695 commits at time of check) while still being an ancestor (not diverged) -- meaning fixes built against a default clone can target already-resolved bugs without any merge-conflict signal to catch the mistake, since the branches never diverged, main just stopped moving forward. Concretely: 4 CI job failures were investigated (a month-old Benchmark Gate run plus a coverage/lint/integration set on main at a specific commit); several real-looking fixes were built and verified against that clone before the branch mismatch was caught via git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/merged. Re-verified against merged's actual current tip: all 4 were already resolved there (a file that no longer exists in that form; a Scan()-vs-column-count mismatch already fixed independently; golangci-lint already clean; the same DB bug feeding the integration failures). The real, current CI status for merged's own tip, checked directly via GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{sha}/check-runs, showed only one job (build-and-push, success) -- the coverage/lint/integration jobs apparently only run on pull requests, not direct pushes to merged, so "merged's CI is green" is a narrower claim than "every job type recently ran and passed." Required discipline before touching any code in response to a reported CI failure in this repo: (1) confirm which branch the failing job's commit actually belongs to -- do not assume a default clone or a branch name in a URL is the right target; (2) check how old the job run is; (3) check the real current tip's own CI status directly via the API before diagnosing, since a local clone's checkout may not match. A smaller, related technical gotcha found along the way: a naive Python .split(",") on a raw SQL column-list string produces a false positive column-count mismatch when the list contains a COALESCE(a, b) AS c expression (comma inside parens) -- any script comparing SQL column lists to Go Scan() destinations in this codebase needs a parenthesis-aware splitter, not a naive one.

decisions.notes: A real, demonstrated mistake this session (fixes built against the wrong branch, caught only after work was already done) with a concrete, generalizable discipline for future upstream AgentsView syncs and periscope remediation work -- directly requested to be recorded.
